content:
Great, all leaf reagents are buyable.

Now we need to design a retrosynthetic route using these leaves, max 6 steps.

Proposed route:

Target (T) = sulfonamide linking aryl (fluorophenyl) to aniline core (tetralin-1-ol with aniline at position). The aniline is attached to piperazine (N-Boc). So steps:

Step 1 (disconnection): Break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (4-fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride) and aniline intermediate (A). Reaction: sulfonyl chloride + aniline -> sulfonamide (target). So leaf: sulfonyl chloride (buyable) and aniline intermediate (A) which we need to synthesize.

Step 2: The aniline intermediate (A) is the tetralin-1-ol core bearing an aniline at appropriate position (maybe 5-aminotetralin-1-ol). We can get it via Buchwald-Hartwig coupling of bromotetralin-1-ol (aryl bromide) with N-Boc-piperazine? Wait the aniline is attached to the tetralin core, not the piperazine. Actually the aniline is part of the tetralin core: the nitrogen of the sulfonamide is attached to the tetralin phenyl ring (the aniline). The piperazine is attached to that same nitrogen? Wait the SMILES: O=S(NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O

Interpretation: Sulfonyl group attached to N which is attached to aromatic carbon (C1). That aromatic carbon is part of a fused ring system (C1=CC(... )=C3...). The N is attached to that aromatic carbon (i.e., an aniline). The N also attached to piperazine? Actually the N is part of sulfonamide, not attached to piperazine. The piperazine is attached to the aromatic ring via a substituent: N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2 is attached to the aromatic carbon (the same aromatic ring) as a side chain (i.e., an aryl-amine substituent). So the aromatic ring has two substituents: the sulfonamide nitrogen (attached via N) and a piperazine side chain (attached via carbon). So the piperazine is attached via a carbon (aryl-alkyl amine) not via nitrogen.

Thus the piperazine is attached via a carbon (aryl-alkyl) as a substituent: the aromatic carbon is attached to N of piperazine (i.e., aryl-N-piperazine). So we need to form C-N bond between aryl carbon and piperazine nitrogen. That's a Buchwald-Hartwig amination (aryl halide + piperazine). So we need aryl halide (bromotetralin-1-ol) and N-Boc-piperazine.

Thus step 2: Buchwald-Hartwig coupling of bromotetralin-1-ol (aryl bromide) with N-Boc-piperazine to give aryl-piperazine (still Boc protected). This yields intermediate B.

Step 3: Deprotect Boc to give free secondary amine (piperazine) (if needed for later steps). But the final target has the piperazine nitrogen bearing a Boc carbamate (tert-butoxycarbonyl) on the other nitrogen, not on the aryl-attached nitrogen. In our intermediate after coupling, the piperazine nitrogen attached to aryl is free (secondary amine) and the other nitrogen is Boc-protected. The target has the other nitrogen carbamated (Boc) as well, which matches. So we need to keep Boc on the other nitrogen, which we already have. The aryl-attached nitrogen is free, which is fine (target has no protecting group there). So we may not need deprotection. Actually the N-Boc-piperazine has Boc on one nitrogen; after coupling, the Boc remains on the other nitrogen. So step 2 yields final piperazine substitution as needed. No further steps needed for piperazine.

Step 4: The aryl bromide (bromotetralin-1-ol) can be derived from tetralin-1-ol via bromination at the appropriate position (e.g., bromination of tetralin-1-ol). So step 3: Bromination of tetralin-1-ol to give bromotetralin-1-ol (aryl bromide). This uses NBS etc. Leaf: tetralin-1-ol (buyable). So step 3 is functionalization.

Step 5: The sulfonyl chloride coupling (step 1) attaches the sulfonyl group to the aniline (which is the aromatic carbon bearing the sulfonamide). The aniline is part of the tetralin core after substitution? Actually after step 2, we have tetralin-1-ol with piperazine attached at a certain position (maybe position 5). The sulfonamide attaches to the same aromatic carbon? Wait the sulfonamide nitrogen attaches to the aromatic carbon (forming an aniline). That carbon is part of the tetralin aromatic ring. So we need to have an aniline (NH2) on the tetralin core at the position where sulfonamide attaches. In the target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the aromatic carbon, not the nitrogen attached to the aromatic carbon. So the aromatic carbon is attached to N (sulfonamide). That means the aromatic carbon is attached to N (forming an aniline). So the precursor before sulfonylation is the aniline (tetralin-1-ol with an amino group at that position). So we need to have an aniline on the tetralin core.

Thus our route must also introduce an amino group onto the tetralin core at the appropriate position (maybe via nitration/reduction). So we need an intermediate C: 5-aminotetralin-1-ol (or similar). Then we can do sulfonylation with sulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide.

Thus we need to generate the aniline from tetralin-1-ol via bromination then amination? Actually we could start from tetralin-1-ol, brominate at the desired position, then do Buchwald-Hartwig amination with ammonia (or protected amine) to give aniline. But we already used Buchwald-Hartwig for piperazine. Could we do a sequential coupling? Might be too many steps.

Alternative: Use a commercially available 5-bromo-1-tetralol (maybe buyable). Let's check if it's buyable.

Search is_buyable for "Brc1ccc2c(c1)C(CCC3(CCC3)O3)=C2"? That's the brominated version of the fused core. Let's test.


Let's call is_buyable for that SMILES.
